title: Add shadow-traffic validation adapter with automated rollback orchestration
author: Aisha Kapoor
release_notes: Added a shadow-traffic validation adapter and automated rollback orchestration that enables safe canary validations against golden prompt sets and a configurable abort policy.
description: Context: Production rollouts have an increasing need to validate model behavior on shadow traffic with deterministic checks before promoting to live traffic. This PR introduces a light-weight shadow validation adapter that runs a configurable suite of checks (SLO/metric thresholds, semantic drift signals, and deterministic prompt-set regression checks) and hooks into the rollout controller to trigger automatic rollback or quarantine when safety gates fail. Motivation: Reduce manual toil for transient regressions and make rollback decisions auditable and consistent across hosted/dedicated/private deployments. Change summary: 1) Add server-side adapter that subscribes to mirrored requests, computes validation signals, and emits decision tokens. 2) Extend the rollout controller with a new 'validation-policy' stage that consumes the adapter decisions and supports timeboxed tolerances, failure budgets, and quarantine windows. 3) Add integration tests, observability metrics, and a docs runbook for incident responders. Checklist: - [x] Implementation of adapter and controller hooks - [x] Unit tests for adapter logic - [x] Integration tests within the canary harness - [x] Prometheus metrics and Grafana dashboard snippets - [x] Runbook and rollback playbook - [x] Security review for request mirroring path Design notes: The adapter processes mirrored requests asynchronously and maintains per-cohort sliding windows for metric aggregation. It supports pluggable validators: threshold, delta-from-baseline, and token-level regression checks. Decisions are signed with the rollout controller's service identity and persisted to the rollout journal so historical rollbacks are reconstructible. Performance consideration: adapter is implemented with a bounded worker pool and priority queue to avoid head-of-line blocking on serving nodes; default flavor samples 1:10 of mirrored traffic for heavy routes to keep cost predictable. Rollout behavior: When the validation-policy fails hard thresholds, the controller will immediately flip canary traffic to fallback and optionally quarantine the model variant; soft failures accumulate into a failure budget which can trigger automated mitigations (e.g. reduce traffic, extend canary). Testing & CI: added integration test harness that runs synthetic shadow traffic, asserts metrics emission and controller decision flow, and runs against a small colocated runtime using qkv-mock model. Observability: metrics prefixed rollout_validation_* (count, error_rate, drift_score), traces instrumented for per-request validation path, and an example Grafana panel in docs. Security & privacy: mirrored payloads are redacted according to existing redaction pipeline before being processed; KMS keys used to sign decisions. Migration: feature-gated by default; rollout-controller config flag 'enableShadowValidation' must be set. Rollout plan: staged rollout to internal tenants for 2 weeks behind a feature flag, then enable for low-traffic customers, progressively widen cohort. Backout: feature flag off or controller rollback. Related: linear ENG-1824 (validation service), ENG-1899 (canary-controller extension), SUP-3328 (customer incident that motivated auto rollback).

notes_for_release: Feature gated behind 'enableShadowValidation'. Opt-in for early customers; recommended to enable only with monitoring dashboards and alert thresholds configured.
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: noisy false positives causing unnecessary rollbacks. Mitigation: conservative defaults, failure budget, quarantine window, audit logs, and a manual override in the console.
test_plan: Unit tests covering validators; integration tests simulate mirrored traffic with golden prompt sets and assert metric thresholds; staging rollout to internal tenants for 2 weeks with canary at 5% then 20% before wide rollout.
